bullets.title: US Optical Transceiver Ban Draft Sparks Major Rally in LITE, COHR, AAOI, CIEN
bullets.body: The Trump administration is reportedly drafting a ban on imports of Chinese optical transceivers and data center components, per Reuters. Coherent surged +14%, Lumentum +11%, and Corning +7.9% in premarket, with traders noting InP laser array supply chains as the key bottleneck. One analyst flagged the ban could slow DC buildout by ~50%, but sees Western optical suppliers as material beneficiaries despite near-term capacity constraints.

bullets.title: Bezos Files to Sell 15M AMZN Shares (~$4.07B); Stock Crosses $3T Market Cap
bullets.body: Jeff Bezos filed to sell up to 15 million Amazon shares worth approximately $4.07B—stock acquired as founder shares in July 1994. Despite the overhang, AMZN crossed $3 trillion market cap for the first time this session, with Stocktwits sentiment having surged 97% ten days prior.

bullets.title: MSFT and AMZN Up 20%+ in a Week, Now 'Well Into Overbought' Territory
bullets.body: A week ago MSFT and AMZN were solidly below their 50-DMAs; both have since gained 20%+ and are now 'well into overbought' territory. GOOGL has moved from 'deep oversold' to 'slightly overbought' over the same period.

bullets.title: TSLA China July Deliveries +37.8% Y/Y to 93,579 Units
bullets.body: Tesla's China July deliveries came in at 93,579 units per CPCA/PCA preliminary data, up 37.8% year-over-year, signaling a strong demand recovery in its largest EV market.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Hits All-Time High; Nasdaq 100 Futures Extend Climb to +1.1%
bullets.body: The S&P 500 (SPY) reached a new all-time high during the session, with Nasdaq 100 futures extending gains to 1.1%. Yesterday marked the first time in 29 months the S&P gained >1% on the first trading day of a month—ending the longest such streak since 1996.

bullets.title: Citadel's Rubner: July Selloff 'Reset the Bull Market, Not Ended It'
bullets.body: Citadel's Scott Rubner says July's sharp selloff and sector rotation cleared excessive positioning—including heavy selling of AI and semiconductor stocks by retail—but the broader bull market uptrend remains intact.

bullets.title: SPX 0DTE Straddle at Historical Lows Despite Elevated Realized Vol
bullets.body: SPX 0DTE straddles pricing at just $25/33 bps—near the lowest levels seen—despite 5-day realized vol running at 20% and a 1.5% SPX move yesterday. The observation: dealers are slamming index vol while buying single-stock calls.

bullets.title: Bessent: Possible Iran Deal to Open Hormuz Tuesday/Wednesday; Algos No Longer Reacting
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent told CNBC a deal to open the Strait of Hormuz could come Tuesday or Wednesday, though Qatar simultaneously said there is no set agenda for direct US-Iran talks. Commentary noted algos have stopped responding to Hormuz deal headlines, with WTI crude later extending losses as much as 4.5% on deal hopes.

bullets.title: Bessent on Yen: BOJ Will Do What's Needed; FIMA Repo as FX Swap Equivalent
bullets.body: Bessent backed Japan's yen stabilization efforts, stating he sees no reason Japan should stop accumulating overseas assets. He also flagged the Fed's FIMA repo facility as functionally equivalent to FX swap lines and 'reasonable' to upsize—a hawkish FX coordination signal. BOJ data suggests no large-scale intervention actually occurred Monday, with USDJPY rebounding nearly 300 pips from intervention lows.

bullets.title: 10Y JGB Auction Posts 'Second Biggest Tail in Two Decades' as Buyers Step Away
bullets.body: Japan's 10-year JGB auction was characterized as having the 2nd largest tail in 20 years as buyers withdrew, raising concerns about stability in Japan's bond market. Yen continues weakening despite intervention efforts.

bullets.title: AAPL India Sales Top $10B for First Time; DZ Bank Downgrades to Hold, PT $310
bullets.body: Apple's annual India sales exceeded $10 billion for the first time, signaling growing EM penetration. Separately, DZ Bank downgraded AAPL from Buy to Hold with a $310 price target. OpenAI also published message exchanges claiming 'Apple is getting this wrong' regarding their integration partnership.

bullets.title: KLA Purchase Commitments Jump from $2.75B to $4.83B in One Quarter
bullets.body: KLA's purchase commitments more than doubled to $4.83B quarter-over-quarter, a sharp break from the 2-5% growth trend seen over the prior two years—suggesting a major acceleration in semiconductor equipment demand.

bullets.title: Barclays: 85% of S&P 500 Beat Q2 Estimates; EPS Up 25.1% YoY Led by Big Tech
bullets.body: Barclays reports 85% of S&P 500 companies beat Q2 earnings estimates versus a 76% historical average, with EPS growing 25.1% YoY and revenue up 11.2% YoY. Big Tech was singled out as the primary driver of outperformance.

bullets.title: SPOT Hits 300M Premium Subscribers; Q3 Revenue Guidance Beats
bullets.body: Spotify crossed 300 million premium subscribers (vs. 299.2M estimate) and delivered Q3 revenue guidance of €5B vs. consensus €4.93B. Q2 revenue was essentially in-line at €4.78B, gross margin beat at 33.4%, and FCF came in at €797M.

bullets.title: BofA Bull & Bear Indicator at Extreme Sell Reading, but Only 63% Accurate
bullets.body: BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator is at one of its most extreme sell readings since 2000. However, the indicator's historical hit rate is only 63%, meaning it is wrong roughly one-third of the time—worth monitoring but not a standalone signal.

bullets.title: 43% of SPY's Yesterday's Rally Came from Just 5 Stocks
bullets.body: Per Hedgeye/T1Alpha data, 43% of the SPY's prior session rally was attributable to just five stocks, underscoring the concentration of index-level momentum.

bullets.title: US Army Reportedly Depleted Most ATACMS and PrSM Long-Range Missiles in Iran Conflict
bullets.body: Reuters reports the U.S. Army has used 'virtually all' of its long-range ATACMS and PrSM missiles over five months of the Iran conflict, raising questions about defense contractor production rates and resupply timelines.

bullets.title: Hormuz Shipping at ~10% of Pre-Conflict Levels; Aramco CEO: 18 Months to Rebuild Inventories
bullets.body: Saudi Aramco's CEO Amin Nasser warned that even if the Strait of Hormuz reopened today, replenishing global oil inventories could take 18 months. Aramco is rerouting crude via its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea; Hormuz shipping has fallen to roughly one-tenth of pre-conflict levels.
